(<https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/23195>) Am currently investigating it, depends on how fast we can find and fix the problem <@&595685821026271242> ^ I have to keep muting this server, otherwise it keeps beeping with spam like now 🙂 ACD is the only channel I have unmuted on this discord 😅 yeah, specific channel unmuting is nice. There is a reason why Erigon discord is invite-only 🙂 Maybe makes sense for this Discord as well Or just add a verification bot 😅 Happy to help Ugh. Verification bots have a tendency to foil regular users more than bots in my experience. The only type of bot that they stop are incredibly generic scripts you can download online that don't have handlers built for them that defeats the verification bot. And even then, it only works if you segregate users, which becomes a bit of a management nightmare in a server this large since *every* channel created must have either verified users allowed into it or non-verified users allowed to it but **never** both (otherwise the verification bot doesn't do anything about DM spam, which is a bigger problem in my experience. https://ethernodes.org/london yeah, i've suggested this in the past as well 🙂 we're still exploring options on how to manage, happy to hear suggestions would suggest to have a verification bot but offline, so you can flip the button if needed surprised this server has not been spammed like mad yet 🙂 what marks a client ready? is there any version out there right now that is "ready" ? <@!489217181104734219> no client has announced a mainnet london release yet Are you certain? Nethermind: "[LONDON] Mainnet chainspec upgrade". Erigon 07-02 alpha also has London block for mainnet defined. Something something "those aren't the cool kids" 🤣 🍿 ... okay never mind 😉 Ahh, I missed those! Thanks <@!219015859182632960> 🙂 I looked on the Nethermind announcement channel this AM actually, but haven't done a proper Github round 🙂 I think, to be fair, both of those are kinda "on the DL" - the releases have the mainnet block defined but aren't being very loud about it. And while I am a bit shaky on that, I don't think either one of those supports mining on London. That'll be Geth/Besu/OE (while we still have it 😿 ) Yep, given the mining-related changes, the announcement will make it clear how miners on Geth/Besu/OE can update their gas target 👍 <@!219015859182632960> do you have a link to the Erigon release with mainnet london blocks? Can't seem to find it... excuse me for being out of the loop here, but is Erigon ready for prime time? and is Erigon what started as Turbo-Geth? is it good as a drop in replacement for geth in a live mainnet validator setup? It is a rename of TurboGeth, and it syncs to mainnet, but I'm not sure if it has all the required features to replace geth when running alongside an eth2 validator thanks <@!552133098075193354> See how I said "on the DL"? Erigon takes that to an extreme. Zero, nada, zilch in release notes, and this on start: `Initialised chain configuration config="{ChainID: 1 Homestead: 1150000 DAO: 1920000 DAOSupport: true EIP150: 2463000 EIP155: 2675000 EIP158: 2675000 Byzantium: 4370000 Constantinople: 7280000 Petersburg: 7280000 Istanbul: 9069000, Muir Glacier: 9200000, Berlin: 12244000, London: 12965000, Engine: ethash}"` Oh, intersting! Thanks for sharing 🙂 Alpha releases. **Not** ready for production IMO. My opinion is technically quite conservative. There is room for differing opinions, for sure. And yes, Erigon was once named "Turbo-Geth" A month ago? More? In Ethereum time, does that equal "years"? 🤣 LOL it feels like years a bit haha Shouldn't the "protocol releases" list on https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs use a more international date format as instead of the American mm/dd/yyyy ? agreed https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs/pull/258 😬 I pushed a PR at the time: https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs/pull/257 Merged <@!543900561460822016>'s PR because it was proper ISO 😛 I'd argue the proper one is yyyy-mm-dd 🙂 second that that's what he did Ok, the time I checked the PR it had yyyy/mm/dd AH, you mean `/` vs. `-` ? ah, I dont care about delimiters I'm out Happy to merge the PR of whoever cares most 🙂
